text:
Maria Chen: heads-up — noticed the cost dashboard is attributing almost all cache savings to the model instead of the calling route for a multi-route customer. looks wrong to me
Kevin Patel: ugh that's bad. is this the shared-prefix cache case? or cache computed after routing?
Maria Chen: shared-prefix + KV cache. runtime emits total_tokens and served_tokens but we currently compute cache_saved by diffing against model's baseline, then apply to model_id only
Natalie Ruiz: that's because telemetry only has model_id + tokens, no route_id on cache metrics. we aggregate by model for rollups
Devon Li: quick idea: add a "cache_credit" telemetry field that includes route_id and model_variant so we can split savings at attribution time
Sam O'Neill: agree, but need to think cross-tenant shared caches. if two routes hit same prefix, who gets the credit? first-touch? weighted by request latency reduction? :thinking_face:
Maria Chen: proposal: 1) emit per-request telemetry: { route_id, model_id, raw_input_tokens, raw_output_tokens, kv_hits, kv_saved_tokens } 2) ingestion job computes credits per request and stores per-route aggregates
Kevin Patel: that seems fine, minimal runtime impact if kv_hits is just an int. we already emit `served_tokens` and `input_tokens`. adding `kv_saved_tokens` as int should be cheap
Natalie Ruiz: UX implications: dashboards should show both gross_token_cost and net_token_cost and a column `cache_savings_allocated` with a note for shared-cache heuristics
Devon Li: FYI edge case: embeddings calls often dedupe at request time (de-duped cache) — attribution should not double-count for batch de-dupe that spans routes
Sam O'Neill: good catch. maybe dedupe tag: `dedupe_window_id` or `dedupe_key_counts` in telemetry to indicate multi-request dedupe so we can attribute proportionally
Maria Chen: example telemetry snippet — feel free to tweak:
```json
{
  "route_id": "search-autocomplete",
  "model_id": "rw-0.9-800m",
  "input_tokens": 120,
  "output_tokens": 40,
  "kv_hits": 1,
  "kv_saved_tokens": 80,
  "dedupe_key": null
}
```
Kevin Patel: ingestion rules roughly:
- if dedupe_key != null => split savings by request count in that dedupe window
- if kv_hit && first_touch_route != null => assign full credit to first_touch_route for that prefix
- otherwise => pro-rata by route token usage in same aggregation period
Natalie Ruiz: we'll need to add a tooltip in the dashboard explaining the heuristic and an audit link to raw telemetry rows (for customers who want to dispute allocation). also add a column for `allocation_method` (first_touch / pro-rata / dedupe-split)
Devon Li: backward compatibility: old telemetry will have no kv_saved_tokens. ingestion should treat missing as 0 and keep existing model-level rollups unchanged for historical continuity
Sam O'Neill: operational note: cost-bot will start a nightly job to recompute per-route credits for the last 30 days after schema change, to backfill; we should surface progress to the dashboard (ETA + errors) :gear:
cost-bot: scheduled job queued: nightly-cache-credit-backfill (start: 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC). will emit progress events to #eng-platform :robot_face:
Maria Chen: next steps: Kevin + Devon to spec telemetry change (runtime side), Natalie to mock dashboard UI with gross/net toggle and allocation_reason column, Sam to wire backfill job and add ETAs. syncing Friday @ 11 to review PRs
Kevin Patel: ok i'll draft runtime patch and feature-flag it behind `emit_kv_savings_v2`
Natalie Ruiz: i'll drop an infra-freeze note if the backfill will touch prod tables; want to avoid query thrash
Maria Chen: thanks all. small follow-up — can we add a tiny column in the per-route CSV export `cache_alloc` so finance can reconcile with billing exports?
Sam O'Neill: yes, will add `cache_alloc` (decimal) to CSV export, and include `allocation_method` in the metadata header
Maria Chen: perfect. that's all for now :thumbsup:
